items.title: Joe Robichaux Interview, 1959-03-19
items.q: It was Ward Crosby. He was a drummer. We used to call him Bucket

ctx.x: We only had six pieces of band. Six? Yeah. There wasn't more than that. No, it was six. We only had the drum, piano.

It was Ward Crosby. He was a drummer. We used to call him Bucket, a little short fella. He lives in Chicago. That's his home. And we had Eugene Ware, Eugene Porter, and I had Alfred Gishard, and Walter Williams. He had no bass. No bass. No trombone. Just six pieces. I don't know. A whole lot of people thought it was more than six pieces for one reason. You see now, the trumpet player, I mean the tenor-psychopone player used to double on trumpet. See he could play trumpet too.
